Sampling options

sampling-options.Rmd

Sampling options

sample_non_events() turns an observed event log into a nested case-control sample: each event (the case, event = 1) is paired with n_controls dyads that could have fired at that moment but did not (the controls, event = 0), and the pair shares a stratum id. The options below decide which dyads count as “could have fired”. This page runs each option on classroom_events or on a small constructed log and shows what changes in the control set. The code runs when the page is built.

data(classroom_events)
ev <- classroom_events
c(events = nrow(ev),
  senders = length(unique(ev$sender)),
  receivers = length(unique(ev$receiver)))
#>    events   senders receivers 
#>       691        18        20

n_controls

The number of controls per case. Every stratum holds one case and up to n_controls controls; a stratum gets fewer only when the risk set has fewer valid dyads than that.

sizes <- sapply(c(1, 3, 10), function(k) {
  cc <- sample_non_events(ev, n_controls = k, seed = 1)
  c(n_controls = k, rows = nrow(cc), controls = sum(cc$event == 0L),
    distinct_control_dyads = length(unique(key(ctrl(cc)))))
})
t(sizes)
#>      n_controls rows controls distinct_control_dyads
#> [1,]          1 1382      691                    321
#> [2,]          3 2764     2073                    379
#> [3,]         10 7601     6910                    380

Controls are drawn with replacement across strata, so the same dyad can serve as a control for many events; with ten controls per case the 6910 controls cover 380 distinct dyads.

mode: one actor pool or two

mode = "one" (the default) draws control senders and receivers from the same pool of actors, as in networks where everyone can both send and receive. mode = "two" draws senders from the actors seen as senders and receivers from the actors seen as receivers, as in bipartite networks.

receiver_only <- setdiff(unique(ev$receiver), unique(ev$sender))
receiver_only
#> [1] "2"  "19"
by_mode <- sapply(c("one", "two"), function(m) {
  cc <- ctrl(sample_non_events(ev, n_controls = 3, mode = m, seed = 2))
  c(controls = nrow(cc),
    control_senders = length(unique(cc$sender)),
    controls_sent_by_receiver_only = sum(cc$sender %in% receiver_only))
})
by_mode
#>                                 one  two
#> controls                       2073 2073
#> control_senders                  20   18
#> controls_sent_by_receiver_only  208    0

In this log 2 actors (2, 19) only ever receive. Under mode = "one" they appear as senders in 208 controls; under mode = "two" in none, because they are not in the sender pool.

scope: who is in the risk set

"all" and "appearance"

scope = "all" uses every actor seen anywhere in the log. scope = "appearance" uses only actors that appeared in an event before the focal event, so an actor who enters late is not at risk early on.

first_seen <- tapply(c(seq_len(nrow(ev)), seq_len(nrow(ev))),
                     c(ev$sender, ev$receiver), min)
not_yet_seen <- function(cc) {
  d <- ctrl(cc)
  sum(first_seen[d$sender] >= d$stratum | first_seen[d$receiver] >= d$stratum)
}
cc_all <- sample_non_events(ev, n_controls = 3, scope = "all",        seed = 3)
cc_app <- sample_non_events(ev, n_controls = 3, scope = "appearance", seed = 3)
rbind(all        = c(controls = sum(cc_all$event == 0L), not_yet_seen = not_yet_seen(cc_all)),
      appearance = c(controls = sum(cc_app$event == 0L), not_yet_seen = not_yet_seen(cc_app)))
#>            controls not_yet_seen
#> all            2073           51
#> appearance     2070            0
seen_before <- vapply(1:40, function(i) sum(first_seen < i), numeric(1))
op <- par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 1, 1))
plot(1:40, seen_before, type = "s", lwd = 2, xlab = "event index",
     ylab = "actors seen before the event", ylim = c(0, 20))
abline(h = length(first_seen), lty = 2, col = "grey50")

par(op)

The step curve counts the actors that have appeared before each of the first 40 events; the dashed line is the 20 actors of the log. Under "all", 51 controls involve an actor who has not yet appeared; under "appearance", 0. All actors have appeared by event 27, so the two scopes differ only at the start of this log. The first event has no earlier events and gets no controls under "appearance" (0 controls in stratum 1).

"citation"

scope = "citation" is built for citation networks, where a paper (the sender) cites earlier papers (the receivers) at its publication time. The control sender is a paper that appears as a sender at the focal time, and the control receiver is a paper that has appeared as a sender earlier, that is, one already published and citing. The citing and the cited paper play different roles, so scope = "citation" always draws them from these two separate pools, whatever mode is set to.

We construct a citation log: 60 papers published at times 1, …, 60, each paper from the second on citing up to three earlier papers at its own publication time.

set.seed(4)
cit <- do.call(rbind, lapply(2:60, function(i) {
  k <- min(3, i - 1)
  data.frame(sender = paste0("p", i),
             receiver = paste0("p", sample(seq_len(i - 1), k)),
             time = i)
}))
head(cit)
#>   sender receiver time
#> 1     p2       p1    2
#> 2     p3       p1    3
#> 3     p3       p2    3
#> 4     p4       p3    4
#> 5     p4       p1    4
#> 6     p4       p2    4
pub_time <- setNames(1:60, paste0("p", 1:60))
cites_future <- function(cc) {
  d <- ctrl(cc)
  sum(pub_time[d$receiver] >= d$time)
}
cc_ca <- sample_non_events(cit, n_controls = 2, scope = "all",      mode = "two", seed = 5)
cc_cc <- sample_non_events(cit, n_controls = 2, scope = "citation", seed = 5)
rbind(all      = c(controls = sum(cc_ca$event == 0L),
                   receiver_not_yet_published = cites_future(cc_ca)),
      citation = c(controls = sum(cc_cc$event == 0L),
                   receiver_not_yet_published = cites_future(cc_cc)))
#>          controls receiver_not_yet_published
#> all           348                        152
#> citation      344                          0

Under "all", 152 of the controls “cite” a paper that is published at or after the citing time; under "citation", 0. Paper p1 cites nothing in this log, so it never appears as a sender and is not a candidate receiver under "citation" except as the focal event’s own receiver.

risk = "remove": one-shot dyads

Some processes fire each dyad at most once: a species establishing in a region, a first citation, a first contact. Under risk = "remove" a dyad that has fired leaves the risk set, so it cannot be a control for any later event. We simulate such a process and round its times to whole units, which creates tied events.

set.seed(6)
os <- simulate_relational_events(
  n_events = 150, senders = paste0("s", 1:10), receivers = paste0("s", 1:10),
  risk = "remove")
os$time <- ceiling(os$time * 10)          # ties: several events per unit
c(events = nrow(os), distinct_dyads = length(unique(key(os))),
  events_in_tied_groups = sum(duplicated(os$time) | duplicated(os$time, fromLast = TRUE)))
#>                events        distinct_dyads events_in_tied_groups 
#>                    90                    90                    81
fired_before <- function(cc) {
  first_t <- tapply(os$time, key(os), min)
  d <- ctrl(cc)
  ft <- first_t[key(d)]
  sum(!is.na(ft) & ft < d$time)
}
concurrent <- function(cc) {
  d <- ctrl(cc)
  sum(paste(key(d), d$time) %in% paste(key(os), os$time))
}
cc_std <- sample_non_events(os, n_controls = 5, risk = "standard", seed = 7)
cc_rm  <- sample_non_events(os, n_controls = 5, risk = "remove",   seed = 7)
cc_rmc <- sample_non_events(os, n_controls = 5, risk = "remove",   seed = 7,
                            exclude_concurrent = FALSE)
rbind("standard"                         = c(fired_before = fired_before(cc_std), concurrent = concurrent(cc_std)),
      "remove"                           = c(fired_before = fired_before(cc_rm),  concurrent = concurrent(cc_rm)),
      "remove, exclude_concurrent = FALSE" = c(fired_before = fired_before(cc_rmc), concurrent = concurrent(cc_rmc)))
#>                                    fired_before concurrent
#> standard                                    212         23
#> remove                                        0          0
#> remove, exclude_concurrent = FALSE            0         22

The first column counts controls whose dyad had already fired before the focal time; the second counts controls that coincide with an event at the same time. Under risk = "standard" 212 controls are dyads that had already fired. Under risk = "remove" none are, and by default (exclude_concurrent = TRUE under "remove") no control is a dyad firing at the focal event’s own time either. With exclude_concurrent = FALSE, 22 controls are such concurrent events: at a tie they are still at risk at that instant, as in the Breslow convention. Under risk = "standard" the default is exclude_concurrent = FALSE.

exclude_pairs: structural exclusions

Some dyads can never fire, for reasons outside the model: a species’ native range, a forbidden transition, a pair that is not in contact. They belong outside the risk set. exclude_pairs takes a two-column table of (sender, receiver) pairs that are never sampled as controls. As an illustration on classroom_events, we exclude every dyad from a student to an instructor:

data(classroom_actors)
instructors <- as.character(classroom_actors$id[classroom_actors$role == "instructor"])
students    <- as.character(classroom_actors$id[classroom_actors$role != "instructor"])
forbidden   <- expand.grid(sender = students, receiver = instructors,
                           stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
nrow(forbidden)
#> [1] 36
to_instructor <- function(cc) {
  d <- ctrl(cc)
  sum(d$sender %in% students & d$receiver %in% instructors)
}
cc_free <- sample_non_events(ev, n_controls = 3, seed = 8)
cc_excl <- sample_non_events(ev, n_controls = 3, seed = 8,
                             exclude_pairs = forbidden)
c(without_exclusion = to_instructor(cc_free), with_exclusion = to_instructor(cc_excl))
#> without_exclusion    with_exclusion 
#>               170                 0

Without the exclusion 170 controls are student-to-instructor dyads; with it, 0. Observed events on excluded dyads stay in the log as cases; the exclusion acts on the controls only.

shift = "exponential": controls at their own times

All the options above give each control its case’s time. A covariate that depends only on time (weather, time of day) then takes the same value for the case and its controls and cannot be estimated. With shift = "exponential" each control is drawn from a time-shifted copy of the process and stored at its own time:

cc_sh <- sample_non_events(ev, n_controls = 1, seed = 9, shift = "exponential")
case_time <- cc_sh$time[cc_sh$event == 1L][match(ctrl(cc_sh)$stratum,
                                                 cc_sh$stratum[cc_sh$event == 1L])]
c(controls = sum(cc_sh$event == 0L),
  at_case_time = sum(ctrl(cc_sh)$time == case_time),
  strata_without_control = length(attr(cc_sh, "shift")$uninformative))
#>               controls           at_case_time strata_without_control 
#>                    691                      0                      0

0 of the 691 controls share their case’s time. The species-invasion vignette and the Estimation guide use this design to estimate global covariate effects.

Summary

Option Values What it changes
n_controls integer controls per case
mode "one" (default), "two" one actor pool, or separate sender and receiver pools
scope "all" (default), "appearance", "citation" every actor, actors seen before the event, or citing papers and earlier papers
risk "standard" (default), "remove" whether a dyad stays at risk after it fires
exclude_concurrent NULL (default), TRUE, FALSE whether dyads firing at the focal time can be controls; TRUE under "remove", FALSE under "standard" by default
exclude_pairs two-column table dyads that are never controls
shift "none" (default), "exponential" controls at the case time, or at their own back-shifted times
